_comment: CROSS-CLIENT CONTRACT. Read verbatim by internal/toolclass/row_subject_test.go (Go) and by the GUI's Vitest suite (frontend/src/lib/tool-row-subject.test.ts). `tool` is the CANONICAL tool name as recorded (internal/antigravity/toolnames.go canonicalises run_command->bash, read_url_content->webfetch, grep_search->grep, view_file->read), `input` is the recorded arguments JSON exactly as the part carries it (agy's OWN key spellings are preserved there: CommandLine, TargetFile, Url, query), and `want` is the EXACT string toolclass.RowSubject(tool, input) returns. A case whose `want` is the empty string asserts that the row shows NO subject rather than a JSON dump or a fabricated one. Do not copy this file: assert against these bytes so the two clients cannot drift.

cases.name: agy run_command renders the COMMAND, from agy's CommandLine key
opencode bash renders the command from its own key — the same row either way
a bare-string bash input IS the command
agy write_to_file renders the PATH, from TargetFile
agy view_file renders the PATH, from the AbsolutePath spelling
agy read_url_content renders the URL, not a JSON dump
agy grep_search with a pattern and no path renders the PATTERN
agy grep_search with a path renders the PATH, not the pattern
agy ask_question (no canonical equivalent) renders its question
an empty input renders nothing at all — never a blank JSON scaffold
a JSON object with no scalar value renders nothing rather than flattening a body
